speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, how long have your symptoms been present, and have you experienced any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of acute watery diarrhea occurring shortly after levofloxacin treatment strongly suggests *Clostridioides difficile* infection. Were you able to check your pulse or blood pressure to see if you are showing signs of dehydration? Additionally, have you noticed any significant changes in your bowel habits since starting the antibiotic?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). Given your recent levofloxacin use, severe watery diarrhea, and abdominal cramping, I am ordering a C. diff toxin assay. REQUEST TEST: C_diff_toxin_assay.
